From 8d3a7dfb801d157ac423261d7cd62c33e95375f8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Oliver Upton <oliver.upton@linux.dev>
Date: Wed, 21 Feb 2024 09:27:31 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: arm64: vgic-its: Test for valid IRQ in
 its_sync_lpi_pending_table()

vgic_get_irq() may not return a valid descriptor if there is no ITS that
holds a valid translation for the specified INTID. If that is the case,
it is safe to silently ignore it and continue processing the LPI pending
table.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 33d3bc9556a7 ("KVM: arm64: vgic-its: Read initial LPI pending table")
Signed-off-by: Oliver Upton <oliver.upton@linux.dev>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240221092732.4126848-2-oliver.upton@linux.dev
Signed-off-by: Marc Zyngier <maz@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/arm64/kvm/vgic/vgic-its.c b/arch/arm64/kvm/vgic/vgic-its.c
index e2764d0ffa9f..082448de27ed 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/kvm/vgic/vgic-its.c
+++ b/arch/arm64/kvm/vgic/vgic-its.c
@@ -468,6 +468,9 @@ static int its_sync_lpi_pending_table(struct kvm_vcpu *vcpu)
 		}
 
 		irq = vgic_get_irq(vcpu->kvm, NULL, intids[i]);
+		if (!irq)
+			continue;
+
 		raw_spin_lock_irqsave(&irq->irq_lock, flags);
 		irq->pending_latch = pendmask & (1U << bit_nr);
 		vgic_queue_irq_unlock(vcpu->kvm, irq, flags);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/arm64/kvm/vgic/vgic-its.c`**
- Added a check after the call to `vgic_get_irq()` to verify if `irq` is valid (i.e., not NULL). 
- If `irq` is not valid, the function will now continue to the next iteration of the loop, effectively ignoring the invalid IRQ and preventing further processing.

### Relationships
The modification in `vgic-its.c` addresses a potential issue where `vgic_get_irq()` could return an invalid descriptor if there is no ITS with a valid translation for the specified INTID. By adding the check for a valid `irq`, the patch ensures that the function `its_sync_lpi_pending_table()` can safely ignore invalid IRQs and continue processing without encountering errors, thus improving the robustness of the IRQ handling in the KVM arm64 virtualization layer. This change is a direct response to the bug identified in the previous commit referenced in the patch.

```c
irq = vgic_get_irq(vcpu->kvm, NULL, intids[i]);
```
Reason:
The function `vgic_get_irq()` may return a NULL descriptor if there is no ITS that holds a valid translation for the specified INTID. If this NULL value is dereferenced in subsequent code, it can lead to crashes or undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!irq)
    continue;
```
Reason:
This check ensures that if `vgic_get_irq()` returns a NULL descriptor, the code will skip the current iteration of the loop and continue processing the next INTID. This prevents dereferencing a NULL pointer and thus avoids potential crashes or undefined behavior.
